Prerequisite: The FortiProxy registered on the FortiCloud support portal with its contract registration code, with a valid FortiCare support contract, and each purchased license and FortiGuard subscription bound to its serial number (in an air-gapped network, the license file downloaded from FortiCloud and uploaded)
What it enables: Updates from FortiGuard, which go only to registered units, and the licenses and subscriptions P3 to P11, whose status the Licenses widget shows
How to put it in place: Enter the registration code in GUI: System > FortiGuard (Enter Registration Code), then check GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget); air-gapped: execute restore manual-license tftp <LICENSE_FILE> <TFTP_SERVER>
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Registering FortiProxy" (licenses are grayed out until the unit is registered), "Ensuring internet and FortiGuard connectivity" (updates are provided to registered FortiProxies), "Licenses widget", "FortiGuard" (FortiCare Support status), and "Licensing in air-gap environments"

Prerequisite: A path from the FortiProxy to the FortiGuard network: DNS servers that resolve fds1.fortinet.com, service.fortiguard.net, and update.fortiguard.net, a default route, and the FortiGuard ports allowed outbound by any filtering device, or override FortiGuard servers; in an air-gapped network, packages uploaded by hand
What it enables: Antivirus, IPS, application control, and DLP package updates, web filter and URL rating queries (including IP-based URL rating and the URL risk score), and FortiToken activation, which queries FortiGuard
How to put it in place: Check with execute ping <FORTIGUARD_FQDN> and diagnose debug rating, and in GUI: System > FortiGuard (Test Connectivity in the Filtering section, and Override FortiGuard Servers); check the default route in GUI: Network > Static Routes
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Ensuring internet and FortiGuard connectivity", "Troubleshooting your installation" (steps 5, 9, and 10), "FortiGuard" (Override FortiGuard Servers), "Registering and activating a hard token" (activation requires a connection to FortiGuard), and "Licensing in air-gap environments"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Web Filtering subscription
What it enables: FortiGuard category ratings in web filter profiles (including the child sexual abuse, terrorism, AI, and cryptocurrency categories, and image-analyzer categorization of images with unknown FortiGuard categories) and the FortiGuard category filter in DNS filter profiles
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, register it (P1), and check its status in GUI: System > FortiGuard (Web Filtering)
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "FortiGuard filter" (to use this service, you must have a valid FortiGuard license), "Create or edit a web filter profile" (if the device is not licensed for the FortiGuard web-filtering service, traffic can be blocked), "Create or edit a DNS filter profile" (a FortiGuard Web Filter license is required), and "Using image-analyzer to categorize images with unknown FortiGuard categories"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard AntiVirus subscription
What it enables: Current antivirus engine and definition updates for antivirus scanning in proxy mode
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, register it (P1), and check the contract expiry dates with diagnose autoupdate versions; status in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "FortiGuard" (AntiVirus: the FortiGuard AntiVirus Service provides fully automated updates) and "Licenses widget"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Outbreak Prevention license
What it enables: FortiGuard Virus Outbreak Protection Service hash queries for files scanned by antivirus profiles, with or without the antivirus engine scan
How to put it in place: Purchase the license, register it (P1), and check the Outbreak Prevention entry in the License Information table in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "FortiGuard Outbreak Prevention" (the FortiProxy unit must be registered with a valid FortiGuard outbreak prevention license) and "Configuring threat feed and outbreak prevention without AV engine scan"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard IPS subscription
What it enables: Current IPS signature database updates for IPS sensors, including rate-based signatures and inline IPS for proxy traffic
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, register it (P1), and check the contract expiry dates with diagnose autoupdate versions; status in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "FortiGuard" (IPS: to update the IPS database, select Upgrade Database) and "Licenses widget" (IPS status)

Prerequisite: A valid FortiGuard subscription for Application Control signature updates (the application control profile itself is free)
What it enables: Current application signatures for application control lists and application group filters
How to put it in place: Register the unit (P1) and check the Application Control Signatures entry in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "FortiGuard" (Application Control Signatures: signature database updates require a valid FortiGuard subscription)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard DLP service license
What it enables: FortiGuard-managed DLP data types, dictionaries, and sensors, and the latest DLP package (custom DLP sensors work without it from 7.4.2)
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, register it (P1), and check it in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Data Loss Prevention" (FortiGuard DLP service: a valid DLP license is required) and the FortiGuard dictionaries use cases (a valid DLP license is required to obtain the latest package); FortiProxy 7.4.2 Release Notes, "DLP license changes"

Prerequisite: A Firmware and General Updates (FMWR) contract
What it enables: Upgrades to a major or minor FortiProxy release, and the Inline-CASB Application Definitions entitlement
How to put it in place: Register the contract (P1) and check the Firmware and General Updates section of the License Information table in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Fabric Management" (a valid FMWR license is a prerequisite for upgrading to a major or minor firmware release) and "Inline CASB" (the Inline-CASB Application Definitions entitlement is licensed under the basic firmware and updates contract)

Prerequisite: A Browser Isolation (FortiNBI) license, and an isolator server and isolator profile for the policy to use
What it enables: Browser isolation of the traffic that a policy sends to the isolator
How to put it in place: Register the license (P1) and check it in GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget); define the isolator server with config web-proxy isolator-server; edit <ISOLATOR_SERVER>; set addr-type ip; set ip <ISOLATOR_IP>; set port <PORT>; next; end; or GUI: Policy & Objects > Isolator Setting > Servers
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "License Sharing Information widget" and "License Usage History widget" (Browser Isolation license type) and "Isolator Setting"; FortiProxy 7.2.5 and 7.2.6 Release Notes (Browser Isolation license)

Prerequisite: FortiClient EMS 7.0.0 or later with ZTNA enabled and a FortiClient EMS fabric connector on the FortiProxy, FortiClient 7.0.0 or later on the endpoints, and a ZTNA agent license entitlement (only some license types support ZTNA)
What it enables: ZTNA tags, device certificates, and device ownership for ZTNA access proxies and policies
How to put it in place: Add the connector with config endpoint-control fctems; edit <EMS>; set status enable; set server <EMS_SERVER>; next; end and check it with diagnose endpoint fctems; or GUI: Security Fabric > Fabric Connectors
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Basic ZTNA configuration components", "Configure a FortiClient EMS connector", and "ZTNA troubleshooting scenarios" (make sure that you have a ZTNA agent license entitlement)

Prerequisite: A FortiSandbox appliance reachable from the FortiProxy; for inline scanning, FortiSandbox 4.4.5 or later reachable on port 4443 (FortiSandbox Cloud does not support inline scanning)
What it enables: FortiSandbox inline scanning and its block action, and the alternate FortiSandbox
How to put it in place: config system fortisandbox; set status enable; set inline-scan enable; set server <FORTISANDBOX>; end
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "FortiSandbox inline scanning"

Prerequisite: A FortiProxy model with a hard disk, or a VM with a log disk
What it enables: Local disk logging, quarantine of files to disk, and download of quarantined files
How to put it in place: Check the disk in GUI: Log & Report > Log Settings (Disk Usage)
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Log settings" (disk logging stores logs on a local disk), "Content disarm and reconstruction for antivirus" (local disk quarantine is possible only on models that contain a hard disk), and "Download quarantined files in archive format" (disk logging capacity or a FortiAnalyzer is required)

Prerequisite: A second FortiProxy of the same hardware model running the same software version (the seat license does not have to be identical), with the heartbeat interfaces connected
What it enables: An active-passive or config-sync HA cluster
How to put it in place: Cable the heartbeat interfaces, check the cluster with diagnose sys ha status; settings in GUI: System > HA
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "HA" (the HA clustering members must be the same hardware model running the same software version)

Prerequisite: The DoD PKI root and intermediate CA certificates (and those of any other approved CA) imported into the FortiProxy trust store
What it enables: Validation of the certificates of administrators, users, and the servers the FortiProxy connects to over TLS (LDAP, RADIUS over TLS, ICAP)
How to put it in place: Import each CA certificate in GUI: System > Certificates (Import, CA Certificate)
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Import a CA certificate" and "Certificates"; rows "CA certificates (trust store)" and "Certificate-based (PKI) administrator login"

Prerequisite: DoD OCSP responders and CRL distribution points reachable from the FortiProxy
What it enables: Revocation checks of administrator, user, and server certificates by OCSP or CRL
How to put it in place: Allow the FortiProxy to reach the OCSP and CRL URLs, and import a CRL by hand where it cannot, in GUI: System > Certificates (Import, CRL)
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 CLI Reference, "config vpn certificate ocsp-server" and "config vpn certificate crl"; FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Import a CRL"; rows "OCSP and CRL checking for certificates" and "Certificate revocation lists (CRL) with automatic update"

Prerequisite: A certificate issued to the FortiProxy by the DoD PKI (from a certificate signing request) and imported as a local certificate
What it enables: The administration server certificate, the secure explicit proxy certificate, and the client certificate for RADIUS over TLS
How to put it in place: Generate a request in GUI: System > Certificates (Create, Generate CSR), have the DoD PKI sign it, and import the signed certificate
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Certificate Signing Requests", "Import a local certificate", and "Secure explicit proxy"

Prerequisite: A DoD-issued subordinate CA certificate and key for SSL deep inspection, imported into the FortiProxy, and its issuing CA in the trusted certificate store of every client
What it enables: SSL deep inspection without certificate warnings, and the inspection that HTTP/2, DNS over TLS and HTTPS, and inline CASB depend on
How to put it in place: Deploy the issuing CA to the client trust stores; import the certificate in GUI: System > Certificates; select it as the CA certificate in GUI: Security Profiles > SSL/SSH Inspection
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Create or edit an SSL/SSH inspection profile" (you need to have the certificate installed in your browser, or you might see certificate warnings) and "Inline CASB" (the policy must use a deep inspection SSL profile)

Prerequisite: DoD PKI certificates (such as the CAC) issued to the administrators and proxy users, with the middleware that presents them in the browser
What it enables: Certificate-based administrator login and client certificate authentication of proxy users
How to put it in place: Issued by the DoD PKI; not a FortiProxy setting
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Basic authentication with cached client certificates"; rows "Certificate-based (PKI) administrator login" and "Client certificate authentication for proxy users"

Prerequisite: The administrator profile that the account will use
What it enables: Least-privilege local, remote, and REST API administrator accounts
How to put it in place: config system accprofile; edit <PROFILE>; set sysgrp read; next; end; or GUI: System > Admin Profiles
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Admin Profiles"; row "Administrator profiles (none, read, read-write per functional area)"

Prerequisite: A RADIUS server (or a RadSec server for RADIUS over TLS) with the FortiProxy defined as a client and a shared secret
What it enables: Remote administrator authentication with RADIUS, and RADIUS over TLS
How to put it in place: Define the FortiProxy as a client on the server, then test with diagnose test authserver radius <RADIUS> <AUTH_TYPE> <USER> <PASSWORD>
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "RADIUS Servers" and "Create or edit a RADIUS server"; rows "Remote administrator authentication with RADIUS" and "RADIUS over TLS (RadSec) client"

Prerequisite: An LDAP directory server reachable over LDAPS, with a bind account and the user and group objects
What it enables: Remote administrator authentication with LDAP, the user database for form and basic authentication schemes, and group lookup for Kerberos authorization
How to put it in place: Create the bind account on the directory, then test with diagnose test authserver ldap <LDAP> <USER> <PASSWORD>
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "LDAP Servers", "Create or edit an LDAP server", and "Create or edit a Kerberos authentication service" (the LDAP server used for authorization)

Prerequisite: A TACACS+ server with the FortiProxy defined as a client and a shared key
What it enables: Remote administrator authentication and authorization with TACACS+
How to put it in place: Define the FortiProxy as a client on the server, then test with diagnose test authserver tacacs+ <TACACS> <USER> <PASSWORD>
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "TACACS+ Servers" and "Create or edit a TACACS server"

Prerequisite: The Windows Active Directory domain controllers, defined on the FortiProxy
What it enables: Agentless NTLM, detection of Active Directory changes, extra servers for domain controllers, and checks of submitted credentials by the antiphishing profile
How to put it in place: config user domain-controller; edit <DC>; set ip-address <DC_IP>; set domain-name <DOMAIN>; set ldap-server <LDAP>; next; end
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Agentless NTLM support"; FortiProxy 7.6.7 CLI Reference, "config webfilter profile" (antiphish authentication by domain controller or LDAP)

Prerequisite: A Kerberos service principal for the FortiProxy in the Active Directory domain, and its keytab (generated with ktpass) uploaded to the FortiProxy
What it enables: Kerberos (negotiate) authentication of explicit and transparent proxy users, including Windows AD cross-forest
How to put it in place: config user krb-keytab; edit <KEYTAB>; set principal <SPN>; set ldap-server <LDAP>; set keytab <KEYTAB_FILE>; next; end; or GUI: User & Authentication > Kerberos
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Kerberos", "Create or edit a Kerberos authentication service" (use the ktpass command to generate the Kerberos keytab), and "Using Kerberos authentication with Windows AD cross-forest"

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider (such as FortiAuthenticator or Microsoft ADFS) with the FortiProxy registered as a service provider, and the IdP certificate imported
What it enables: SAML authentication of proxy users
How to put it in place: Exchange metadata with the IdP, then config user saml; edit <SAML_SP>; set idp-entity-id <IDP_ENTITY_ID>; set idp-single-sign-on-url <IDP_SSO_URL>; set idp-cert <IDP_CERT>; next; end; or GUI: User & Authentication > SAML
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "SAML" and "Create or edit a SAML server"

Prerequisite: An OpenID Connect identity provider with the FortiProxy registered as a relying party (client ID and secret)
What it enables: OIDC authentication of proxy users
How to put it in place: Register the FortiProxy at the IdP, then config user oidc; edit <OIDC>; set issuer <ISSUER>; set client-id <CLIENT_ID>; set client-secret <CLIENT_SECRET>; next; end; or GUI: User & Authentication > OIDC
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "OIDC"

Prerequisite: A Fortinet Single Sign-On collector agent on the Windows domain
What it enables: FSSO user identity for proxy policies
How to put it in place: Install the collector agent; check the connection with diagnose debug authd fsso server-status
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 CLI Reference, "config user fsso" (the FSSO collector agent server); FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Create or edit an authentication scheme" (FSSO agent)

Prerequisite: FortiTokens registered and activated on the FortiProxy (hard tokens, or the two free trial mobile tokens)
What it enables: FortiToken two-factor authentication of administrators and users
How to put it in place: config user fortitoken; edit <TOKEN_SERIAL>; set status active; next; end (activation queries FortiGuard, P2); or GUI: User & Authentication > FortiTokens
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "FortiTokens" (only the two free trial mobile tokens can be used) and "Registering and activating a hard token"

Prerequisite: An authentication rule that matches the users' traffic and points to the authentication scheme
What it enables: The authentication scheme and the rule settings, which take effect only through a rule
How to put it in place: GUI: Policy & Objects > Authentication Rules; row "Authentication schemes and rules for proxy users"
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Authentication Rules" (rules point to schemes through active-auth-method and sso-auth-method)

Prerequisite: The explicit web proxy enabled on the internal interface, and the clients' browsers set to use it (the interface address and proxy port, or a PAC file)
What it enables: The explicit proxy, its policies, and its settings, which apply only to traffic that the clients send to the proxy
How to put it in place: Push the browser proxy settings or the PAC URL to the clients; row "Explicit web proxy (HTTP and HTTPS)"
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Explicit web proxy concepts" (users must add the IP address of the interface and the proxy port to their browsers' proxy settings) and "PAC Policy"

Prerequisite: The FortiProxy in the traffic path for transparent proxying: installed inline (NAT/route or transparent mode), or the traffic redirected to it by policy routes or WCCP
What it enables: Transparent proxy policies, which see only traffic that passes through the FortiProxy
How to put it in place: Network design; not a FortiProxy setting
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Transparent and NAT/route modes", "Transparent web proxy concepts", "Policy routes", and "WCCP"

Prerequisite: A policy that matches the traffic and applies the row's profile, profile option, or policy setting
What it enables: Profile and policy settings, which take effect only on the traffic of a policy that uses them
How to put it in place: GUI: Policy & Objects > Policy; row "Security profiles applied in policies"
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Explicit web proxy concepts" (web-proxy policies apply authentication, logging, and security profiles) and "Create or edit a policy"

Prerequisite: The security profiles that the policy names (SSL/SSH inspection, antivirus, web filter, IPS, application control, inline CASB, or LLM)
What it enables: Policies that apply security profiles
How to put it in place: The profile rows of the feature map (for example "SSL deep inspection with certificate checks" and "Antivirus scanning in proxy mode")
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Create or edit a policy"; the profile rows of the feature map

Prerequisite: An ICAP server (or a group of them) that scans the content, defined as an ICAP remote server
What it enables: ICAP content analysis, its failure actions, timeout, load balancing, health checks, and scan size limit
How to put it in place: config icap remote-server; edit <ICAP_SERVER>; set ip-address <ICAP_IP>; next; end
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "ICAP Remote Server" and "Create or edit an ICAP remote server"

Prerequisite: An HTTP or HTTPS server that publishes each threat feed as a plain text file
What it enables: IP address, domain name, URL list, and malware hash threat feeds, and the external block list in antivirus profiles
How to put it in place: Publish the file; check its status in GUI: Security Fabric > External Connectors
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Threat feeds" (FortiProxy imports external threat intelligence lists from an HTTP or HTTPS server) and "Configuring threat feed and outbreak prevention without AV engine scan"

Prerequisite: A syslog server that accepts reliable syslog over TLS
What it enables: Remote syslog of FortiProxy logs, and the JSON and custom syslog formats
How to put it in place: Configure the server for TLS; row "Remote syslog over TLS"
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 CLI Reference, "config log syslogd setting" (mode reliable, enc-algorithm); row "Remote syslog over TLS"

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer that has authorized the FortiProxy
What it enables: Encrypted, reliable, real-time logging to FortiAnalyzer and its log caching
How to put it in place: Authorize the device on the FortiAnalyzer, then check with execute log fortianalyzer test-connectivity
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Logging to FortiAnalyzer" and "FortiAnalyzer log caching"

Prerequisite: An SMTP server that accepts mail from the FortiProxy, and the ISSO mailbox
What it enables: Alert email and email actions of automation stitches
How to put it in place: config system email-server; set server <SMTP_SERVER>; set security smtps; end
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "Email alerts" and "Email Alert Settings"

Prerequisite: Authoritative NTP servers with SHA-256 authentication keys shared with the FortiProxy
What it enables: Authenticated time synchronization
How to put it in place: Share the key ID and key with the NTP server administrator; check with diagnose sys ntp status
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 CLI Reference, "config system ntp" (authentication, key-type, key, key-id); row "NTP time synchronization with authentication"

Prerequisite: An SNMPv3 manager with the matching user, authentication, and privacy settings
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and traps, including the certificate expiration trap
How to put it in place: Configure the user on the manager and list it as a notify host in GUI: System > SNMP
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 Administration Guide, "SNMP" and "Create or edit an SNMP user"

Prerequisite: A FortiManager that manages the FortiProxy
What it enables: Central management, configuration revisions, and backups on FortiManager
How to put it in place: Add the device on the FortiManager; check with diagnose fdsm central-mgmt-status
Source: FortiProxy 7.6.7 CLI Reference, "config system central-management"; row "Central management with FortiManager"
